According to traders, spot premiums for imported copper cathode remain at low levels. Most deals have been struck with premiums in the US$40-50/t range, while the lowest saw a premium of US$20/t. High stocks and weak demand continue to contribute to the negative SHFE/LME arbitrage and has favoured copper exports. However, the loss on cathode imports has weakened over the past fortnight, falling from US$639/t on 27th April to US$333/t on 9th May. Import traffic has been slightly subdued compared to the previous record-setting months, preliminary customs data indicates that wrought and unwrought copper imports amounted to 375,000t in April, down from 462,000t and 485,000t in March and February respectively. Concurrently, SHFE stocks of © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **May 2012** www.crugroup.com cathode have been approximately flat, but Shanghai bonded warehouse inventories have been rising. We estimate that these stocks rose by 120,000t, 90,000t and 50,000t in February, March and April. Our sources say that the past two weeks have seen an additional 50,000t of stocking, leaving Shanghai bonded warehouse inventories totalling 650,000t. CRU maintains the opinion that high import levels seen in the year so far are the result of the requirement to stockpile copper cathode in Chinese warehouses in order to provide collateral for cheaper financing and interest rate plays. However, we suspect that the large and sustained negative arbitrage is now discouraging this activity from growing in prominence. Imports have therefore decelerated from March to reflect this and also the continuing weak underlying demand for copper cathode. We believe that imports of cathode will continue to weaken in May and any pick-up in the rate of bonded warehouse stocking is likely to be the result of further weakness in demand. As noted above, exports of copper cathode have been strongly encouraged by the negative arbitrage. The latest March data indicates exports amounted to 26,537t, up from 700t and 51t in February and January and the highest level seen since April 2011 (44,595t). Another important factor supporting exports is the low levels of stocks in LME warehouses as demand has been picking-up in the World ex-China. We understand that large

r copper smelters and copper traders are exporting or have plans to export copper cathode from China, with April and May outbound trade expected to be well above normal levels. We predict that April will see figures in the range of 50,000t to 90,000t and exports in May could well be of a similar magnitude. # Reversing the China/LME stock imbalance There are currently two major approaches to exporting refined copper from China. The first method entails exporting material from bonded warehouses. Re-exporting material from bonded warehouses is the fastest and most inexpensive means of moving material out of China. Trading companies are the most likely candidate for using this means of trade as they regularly move copper cathode via bonded warehouses. However, material stored in bonded warehouses may also be bought and sold, making this option open to smelters and other interested parties. The other way to export copper cathode from China is via tolling, i.e. the import of copper concentrates for the purpose of exporting copper cathode. From 2006 to 2009, smelters were deterred from doing this as both concentrate imports and refined copper exports were taxed, which meant that smelters undergoing tolling would have paid 17% import VAT plus an additional 3% VAT on the refined copper for export. On 1st February 2009, the seven largest smelters in China were granted tax exemption status for the 17% VAT on their copper concentrate imports for tolling purposes. Exports of refined copper, however, are still charged at 3% VAT. We also understand that there was an additional rule imposed on those tolling smelters granted with a relaxation in their concentrate import tax status, which limited their tax-free concentrate imports for tolling to 20-30% of each smelter’s previous year concentrate import total. We have outlined the maximum possible taxfree concentrate imports and the associated cathode exports in 2012 based around the impacted companies’ import levels in 2011. We expect that these companies, which accounted for around 70% of the total imported copper concentrates in 2011, will increasingly take advantage of their tolling quota in Q2 due to weakened domestic demand for refined copper and tight supplies elsewhere in the world. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 5 **May 2012** www.crugroup.com Maximum possible tax-free copper concentrates imports in 2012

# Sustained slowdown in copper semis-fabrication Information from traders and downstream copper and copper alloy product manufacturers suggests that demand for copper cathode is still weak at present in China. April semi-fabricated product output is understood to have been depressed, with no year-on-year growth expected. Industry participants perceived only a slight up-tick in cathode demand in April from March, after a higher differential had been anticipated. Furthermore, sentiment remains negative about the prospect of any m-o-m growth in demand in May. This viewpoint is strengthened by the knowledge that traditionally, air conditioner manufacturers tend to prepare stocks before summer, causing a seasonal drop in copper tube production from May. We understand that this sector has been well-stocked since the beginning of the year and the utilisation rates of air conditioner manufacturers have already seen a decline of around 10% m-o-m in May. This sector is therefore unlikely to support growth in the coming months. Indeed, when considering copper demand by segment, it seems that copper tube is likely to suffer the greatest growth slow-down this year, but wirerod may perform relatively better. Even so, we believe that the larger wirerod producers experienced scant growth in May compared to the previous month, although with the capacity increases seen in the past year, it is increasingly difficult to gauge whether such views reflect a shrinking market share or weaker end-use demand. We intend to monitor the situation closely in the coming months. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 5 **May 2012** www.crugroup.com # Copper prices seesaw SHFE 3-month price SHFE inventory continues to decline

The official LME cash copper price increased to US$8,530/t on 30th April as the cash-to-3 month backwardation widened to over $150/t and continued to squeeze traders holding short positions on the exchange. However, the price then fell towards $8,000/t on the back of anti-austerity parties winning in the elections in Greece and Francois Hollande winning the Presidency in France, as well as a poor employment report in the USA. The continued weakness in Chinese demand and lower import levels helped to trim stock levels on SHFE. As a result, cathode inventory in SHFE warehouse

s declined by a further 17,000t over the past two weeks.  The fall to 187,449t on 11<sup>th</sup> May took stocks down to a level not seen since the beginning of February.  SHFE prices rose on the first day back from the May 1<sup>st</sup> holiday with the cash month up to RMB58,650/t.  However, prices subsequently fell in sympathy with the LME and a small backwardation between the cash month and 3 month price opened up.  Given the poor demand in China already priced into the SHFE-LME arbitrage, copper prices on SHFE are expected to continue to trade in a RMB56,000-59,000/t range in reaction to developments on the LME and wider macroeconomic news.
